lead.hed: San Antonio came home to Norfolk after a 4th Fleet deployment
lead.insight: DVIDS posted Friday a Navy photo of a sailor hugging a loved one as the amphibious transport dock USS San Antonio returned to Naval Station Norfolk. The official release says the ship came home Oct. 13 after leaving Norfolk on June 29, with Marines and relief supplies, for the U.S. 4th Fleet area. Capt. Matt Gleason, the commanding officer, said the crew had made two deployments in a little over fourteen months. The photo was taken and posted Oct. 16.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Oscar Pichardo · DVIDS 10028646 · Public domain · A sailor assigned to USS San Antonio (LPD 17) hugs a loved one during the ship's return to Naval Station Norfolk. Photo taken and posted Oct. 16, 2026.

political.hed: The Army published a plan for a long fight along the First Island Chain
political.insight: USNI News reported Friday that the Army's new warfighting guidance, released this month, lays out how the service would prepare for a prolonged fight in the Pacific along the First Island Chain. For decades, USNI wrote, the ground branch has oriented troops against insurgent threats and high-intensity combat from the Middle East.

political.hed: Heritage says the Trump-Xi summit bought time and kept leverage
political.insight: Friday's Heritage report covers Chinese General Secretary Xi Jinping's Sept. 23–25 visit to Washington for a summit with President Donald Trump. An earlier Heritage analysis had expected tactical agreements, not a breakthrough. The report says the outcomes that followed bought time and preserved American leverage.

political.hed: American Reformer says America is reacting to a global order coming apart
political.insight: Friday's American Reformer essay says the plates of the global order started moving hard in the 2010s and have not settled. It argues that blaming Donald Trump and MAGA misses the point: in most respects they are reacting to events, not controlling them. American power is real, the piece says, and still not enough to hold a system that is coming apart.

tech.hed: The Army cased the colors of the 8th Psychological Operations Group
tech.insight: Defense News reported Friday that the Army inactivated the 8th Psychological Operations Group (Airborne) in a ceremony at Fort Bragg on Sept. 29. The Army's own release says Col. Robert Cusick and Command Sgt. Maj. Jason Montesanto cased the colors, and that inactivation keeps the unit's people and work inside the Psychological Operations Regiment rather than dissolving them. The group was formally activated on Nov. 16, 2013.

tech.hed: Defense News says the order to slow Starshield for Ukraine came from the White House
tech.insight: Defense News, citing Reuters, reports that two U.S. officials and a Western official said the order to limit SpaceX's Starshield service for Ukraine came from inside the White House. Defense Department leaders were told the service needed to be slowed. The officials did not name who decided. Ukrainian officials said military-grade terminals stopped working on fast-moving objects, which hit drones that use them for guidance. A Ukrainian Defence Ministry person said Thursday the terminals were working again in motion, but only up to 100 miles per hour.

culture.hed: WORLD reports the Muellers still have no grave for Kayla
culture.insight: WORLD reports that Carl and Marsha Mueller wrote President Donald Trump on Nov. 6, 2025, before his meeting with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, asking for help bringing their daughter home. ISIS took Kayla Mueller hostage in Syria on Aug. 4, 2013, and reported on Feb. 6, 2015, that she had been killed. The couple told WORLD they have no grave and no marker. The Foley Foundation, cited in the same piece, reports at least 38 American citizens held by terror groups or hostile governments.

watch.hed: Theodore Roosevelt is the first visiting carrier to dock at Yokosuka in four years
watch.note: USNI's Friday Western Pacific Pulse says the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group docked Friday at Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka, the first time in four years a carrier that is not forward-deployed there has done so. The same feed's Keen Sword item names the cruiser Chosin and the destroyer Decatur alongside the carrier, docked at 9:20 a.m. local time Friday.
